abed-nego.title: Abed-nego
abed-nego.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
abed-nego.note: The Babylonian name they gave Azariah when he was taken into Nebuchadnezzar's service. He is one of the three who would not bow to the golden image and came out of the furnace untouched.

ahasuerus.title: Ahasuerus
ahasuerus.about: Emperor Xerxes I, living at the time of Exile and Return
ahasuerus.note: The Persian king who deposed Vashti and made Esther his queen. He is usually identified with Xerxes the First, whose reign is documented independently in Greek and Persian sources.

arioch.title: Arioch
arioch.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
arioch.note: The captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard, sent to kill Babylon's wise men, and the man Daniel talked into giving him time.

ashpenaz.title: Ashpenaz
ashpenaz.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
ashpenaz.note: He ran Nebuchadnezzar's court eunuchs and picked out young Judean nobles to train for royal service in Babylon, Daniel and his three companions among them.

azariah-2.title: Azariah
azariah-2.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
azariah-2.note: Abednego's birth name. He was one of Daniel's three friends thrown into the fiery furnace in Babylon for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

babylon.title: Babylon
babylon.note: The Mesopotamian empire that destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off. Later Scripture, Revelation included, uses its name as shorthand for worldly power.

belshazzar.title: Belshazzar
belshazzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
belshazzar.note: He ruled Babylon during the exile, and almost all the Bible gives of him is one night: the handwriting on the wall of his banquet hall in Daniel 5. Scripture calls him Nebuchadnezzar's son.

belteshazzar.title: Belteshazzar
belteshazzar.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
belteshazzar.note: Daniel's Chaldee name, given him by Nebuchadnezzar, meaning Beltis protect the king.

chaldean.title: Chaldean
chaldean.note: Originally a tribal people of southern Mesopotamia who went on to found the Neo-Babylonian Empire under Nabopolassar and his son Nebuchadnezzar II. Their armies destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

cyrus.title: Cyrus
cyrus.about: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
cyrus.note: The Persian king who took Babylon and let the deported peoples, the Jews among them, go home and rebuild their temples. Isaiah calls him by name long before he was born, God's shepherd and anointed. The Cyrus Cylinder, found in Babylon in 1879, records the same policy.

daniel.title: Daniel
daniel.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
daniel.note: Carried off to Babylon as a young noble of Judah and renamed by his captors, he rose to high office under three empires without giving up his faith. That refusal got him a night in the lions' den. The visions he received run to the book's last chapter.

darius-2.title: Darius
darius-2.about: Ruler living at the time of Exile and Return
darius-2.note: In Daniel he rules Babylon right after it falls, and he is the king who signed, without wanting to, the decree that put Daniel in the lions' den. Daniel calls him Darius the Mede.

dura.title: Dura
dura.note: Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden image on this plain near Babylon, and Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refused to bow to it. The name probably comes from an Akkadian word for a walled enclosure, so it is more a kind of place than one spot, and no site has been fixed.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elam.title: Elam
elam.note: A kingdom east of Babylon. In the prophets it is one of the nations among which God scattered Israel. Its people turn up again at Pentecost.

gabriel.title: Gabriel
gabriel.note: Daniel meets him first, explaining the visions of coming empires. In Luke he announces two births, John's to Zechariah and Jesus's to Mary, and tells Zechariah he is the one who stands in the presence of God. He is one of only two angels the Bible names.

hananiah-2.title: Hananiah
hananiah-2.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
hananiah-2.note: A prophet who told the exiles the yoke of Babylon would break in two years. Jeremiah told him he was wrong and he died that same year.

hiddekel.title: Hiddekel
hiddekel.note: The Tigris, under its Hebrew name. It is one of the four rivers out of Eden, running east of Assyria, and Daniel is standing on its bank when his last vision comes.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jehoiakim.title: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiakim.note: Pharaoh Necho put him on Judah's throne. When Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, he cut it off a section at a time and burned it in the fire pot, while his advisors begged him to stop. Jeremiah had it written out again, with more added.

jeremiah.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah.note: A priest's son from Anathoth, called as a young man in Josiah's thirteenth year. For four decades he told Judah Babylon was coming, and for that he was jailed, dropped in a cistern, and had his scroll burned. He saw Jerusalem fall as he had said, then was dragged off to Egypt against his will. His scribe Baruch may be the Berekhyahu on a clay seal from his lifetime.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jew.title: Jew
jew.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
jew.note: The word comes from Judah. At first it meant someone from the kingdom of Judah, and after the exile it came to cover the whole covenant people descended from Abraham, whatever tribe they came from.

jewry.title: Jewry
jewry.note: An older English word for Judea, used a few times in the King James Version for the Jewish homeland.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

melzar.title: Melzar
melzar.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
melzar.note: Not really a name. It is the title of the Babylonian official, something like a steward, who had charge of what Daniel and his three friends ate, and some translations simply call him the steward.

mene.title: Mene
mene.note: First word of the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast, and Daniel reads it as numbered.

meshak.title: Meshak
meshak.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
meshak.note: Mishael's Babylonian name. He was one of Daniel's three friends, and they came out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace unhurt after refusing to bow to the golden image.

michael.title: Michael
michael.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
michael.note: Daniel names him as Israel's protector in heaven, standing against the angel princes of Persia and Greece. He is an archangel. Jude has him disputing with the devil over Moses' body, and in Revelation he leads heaven's armies against the dragon.

mishael.title: Mishael
mishael.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
mishael.note: One of Daniel's three friends. In Babylon he was renamed Meshach, and he lived through Nebuchadnezzar's furnace after refusing to worship the golden image.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

no.title: No
no.note: Nahum points to the fall of No, the Hebrew name for the Egyptian city of Thebes, as a warning to Nineveh that no city is too strong for God's judgment.

persia.title: Persia
persia.note: The empire that took Babylon under Cyrus. Unlike the empires before it, Persia let the exiled Jews go home and rebuild their temple, and Ezra keeps the decree.

persian.title: Persian
persian.note: Darius the Persian, whose reign is the marker for when the priestly and Levitical family records in Nehemiah 12 were brought up to date.

shadrach.title: Shadrach
shadrach.about: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
shadrach.note: The Chaldean name given to Hananiah. He was one of the young captives Nebuchadnezzar carried off to Babylon, and he and his two friends would not bow down to the king's image.

shinar.title: Shinar
shinar.note: The old name for the land of Babylon. The tower of Babel went up there, and much later it was the heart of Nebuchadnezzar's empire.

shushan.title: Shushan
shushan.note: The Persian winter capital, east of the Tigris in what is now southwestern Iran, and the Greeks called it Susa. Most of the book of Esther happens here.

ulai.title: Ulai
ulai.note: Daniel stood by the Ulai, near Susa, when he saw the ram and the goat. It is identified with the Eulaeus, a channel of the river system there.

uphaz.title: Uphaz
uphaz.note: Gold from Uphaz overlays idols in Jeremiah and belts the figure in Daniel's vision. Nobody knows where it was, and it may just be a variant of Ophir.
